They may be tried in patients with mild to moderate disease.1,2,4 In- tramuscular gold therapy has also been used for pemphi- gus vulgaris, and might be considered when other adjunc- tive drugs cannot be used.2 High-dose intravenous immunoglobulin has been given to permit reduction of corticosteroid therapy in pemphigus and pemphigoid, and in some patients has produced prolonged remission.8 It is usually reserved for severe disease that has not responded to other therapies.2,4 There have been a few reports of rituximab inducing remission in previously unresponsive pemphigus.3 Plasmapheresis (plasma exchange) may be tried in severe, unresponsive disease,1,2 but there is little evidence of benefit and its use can be limited by cost and adverse effects.4 1.
